title: Fault containment and the error model: one fatal path, one refusal shape, one error space, and hostile-input discipline
summary:
The kernel has one good example of each thing the brief asks for, and none of them is applied as a rule.
- **One fatal path:** the stack-overflow panel costs 174 bytes on kern_big and is safe to draw, but it handles only stack overflow. Divide faults go to the BIOS stub: on a 5150 it masks every IRQ (wm.inc:8280), and on a 286+ the `div` re-runs for ever.
- **One refusal shape:** XREFUSE answers AX=1, but elsewhere CF is the only part a refusal has in common.
- **One error space:** only FERR has a text door.
- **Hostile input:** the 17-rule BPB table is the model to follow; elsewhere fences are per site.

Proposals, in order:
1. Point int 0, and int 6 on a 286+, at the generalised death panel: about +40/+55 resident, +12/+20 `.ovl`. It turns wm-1, loader-4, dw-1, a new FSX_SPK N=0 bug and every package divide into a named stop.
2. Record an owner decision: close the faulting package (the DOS/UNIX two-tier model) rather than stop the machine, about +45..+65 resident.
3. A zero-byte fast-tier ratchet registering every div/idiv with its proof. 5 of ~90 kernel divide sites are unfenced, and all 5 trust a value that crossed a boundary.
4. A MAX column in SYSTEM.CFG's map (0 resident). It retires sysmisc-2 in general.
5. One error CLASS, DOS 59h style, written into the SDK; not one renumbered error number space.
6. A concrete APICHK knob, 0 shipped bytes.

Seven doc/code mismatches recorded.

strengths.title: BPB 17-rule table plus per-call quotient guards
strengths.why: The reference implementation of 'every byte off a disk is hostile': one reader validates, every consumer trusts proven fields. disk_read still refuses an oversized quotient after the mount has validated the BPB.

strengths.title: fsk_needcl saturates instead of faulting on a hostile FileSize
strengths.why: This is the exact guard dw-1 says the write layer lacks. The fix pattern is already in the tree.

strengths.title: Table dispatch and colour xlat are bounded everywhere they were read
strengths.why: ui_cmd's wrap-and-compare, clk_rtc_write, toast_say's unsigned bound, osapi_ferr_text's 'a hostile code above 0x7FFF', and 'and al,15' before every xlatb. A wild index cannot leave a table.

strengths.title: The death panel's construction
strengths.why: It moves SP off the dead stack first, disarms the clip, takes no lock and uses one font_run pass. That is 174 bytes .text + 4 .bss on kern_big (173 on small): a shared body any fatal cause can use.

strengths.title: kern_mega's fault containment model
strengths.why: A package's own fault unwinds to the innermost catch, a worker is killed, a kernel fault stays fatal, and a loop guard limits repeat incidents. This is OS/2 1.x's per-process kill, done properly.

strengths.title: DOS banks IVT 00h per world, and BOOT_MARK already wrote the stub shape
strengths.why: A kernel int 0 handler needs no change to DOS: it becomes the desktop's copy. The 4-byte stub shape and its exclusions (not NMI, not 8 and up) already exist behind a knob.

findings.title: One fatal path: point int 0 (and #UD on a 286+) at the death panel
evidence: kernel/ctrl.inc:5966-5975 (shipped divide overflow from a click)
findings.recommendation: Ship the vector-0 stub on both kernels and the gated vector-6 stub on kern_big. Generalise sch_diepanel to take SI = message and AX/DX = the evidence word(s); print 'DIVIDE ERROR TASK nn AT cccc:iiii NAME'. Add a soak row (a tests/ package dividing by zero in a callback) on MartyPC GLaBIOS and as box-<row> on an 86Box 286, and check it times out when the install is removed.
findings.bytes_est: ~+40 resident kern_small, ~+55 kern_big (with #UD), +12 .ovl (+8 more for vector 6), ESTIMATED
findings.listed_as: not in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE; same proposal as isr-8 and histsys-2, scoped and priced here
findings.prior_art: DOS int 0 'Divide overflow'; Mac SysError bomb box with an ID; OS/2 trap screen; Win 3.0 UAE
findings.verify_note: Re-read: nothing writes IVT 0 (or 1, 3-7) on kern_big or kern_small outside BOOT_MARK's mark_hook (kernel.asm:7721-7752, mark_fvec 0,1,3,4,5,6,7); the comments at instance.inc:1984, ctrl.inc:5980-5982 and wm.inc:8264-8275 all say no handler is installed. The 286+ half is architectural: #DE pushes the IP OF the div, so the BIOS dummy's IRET re-runs it. The 5150 masking claim rests on the tree's own note (wm.inc:8268-8275); the reviewer's open question about the 1986 XT BIOS revision stands. The panel body the stub would join is 174 bytes on kern_big (sch_stkdie 53AE to sch_stkbase 545C, strings included) and 173 on kern_small, matching the maps. Not in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE; same proposal as isr-8/histsys-2, both verified. Byte figures are estimates.

findings.title: A package's own divide fault should close the package, not the machine
evidence: kernel/mega.inc:2504-2560 (mega_fkill: package fault closes the package)
kernel/sched.inc:2580-2583 ('a halted machine is a bug report')
findings.recommendation: Record as an owner decision before gfce-1 ships, because it decides what the panel is for: halt as a bug report, or the app dies and the desk lives.
findings.bytes_est: ~+45 to +65 resident on top of gfce-1, ESTIMATED
findings.prior_art: SIGFPE vs panic(); DOS int 0 terminate; Win 3.0 UAE; OS/2 1.x per-process trap kill
findings.verify_note: A design decision to record, not a defect. mega_fkill (mega.inc, after mega_fault at ~2475-2510) is the precedent: a package fault closes the package on kern_mega. 8086/8088 #DE pushes the address after the div, so the 286+ skip decoder is the only extra code. The estimate is plausible; unmeasured.

findings.title: The divide fence is a habit; make it a ratchet
findings.recommendation: Add tests/unit/t_divsites.py (fast) and tests/divsites.txt. Register every div/idiv in kernel/ and drivers/ by file and label with a reason: const, fenced <label>, validated <rule> or kernel-only. A new divide fails the build until it is registered, and the 'unfenced' count only goes down. It can also carry xlat and computed jumps.
findings.verify_note: Counts reproduced: 95 div, 1 idiv, 7 xlatb in kernel/*.inc and kernel.asm; 48 div/idiv in drivers/. The named unfenced sites exist (current lines wm.inc:7263, diskw.inc:3177 and 3939, deskmod.inc:257, snd.inc:1121, fsx.inc ~4010). One of the five, FSX_SPK's N, is unfenced BY CONTRACT (see gfce-4), so a ratchet must register it as 'trusted by ruling' rather than as a gap. 0 shipped bytes is correct for a host-side gate.

findings.title: OSAPI_FSX_SPK divides by the caller's N with interrupts off
findings.detail:
osapi_fsx_spk (kern_big) documents 'DX = N ... not checked here: packages are trusted', then does mov bx,dx / xor dx,dx / div bx under IF=0. kern_mega's rms_spk does the same. N=0 is a divide by zero:
- on a 286+ it spins at IF=0 after the PIT was reprogrammed, a dead machine;
- on an 8088 it continues, trims sch_rdiv by a garbage remainder and moves the clock.

Any N >= 1 is safe.
evidence: kernel/snd.inc:1073-1074 ('not checked here: packages are trusted')
findings.recommendation: test dx,dx / jz to a new SPK_E_ARG = 2 at both doors; abilock --update without a bump (a code added).
findings.verify_note: The divide is real (snd.inc:1112-1121 mov bx,dx / xor dx,dx / div bx; rms_spk the same in fsx.inc), but leaving N unchecked is a recorded decision, not a bug: SPEC.md 34.11.1 says 'N must be 74..255 ... the door does not re-check it: packages are trusted (the owner's ruling, docs/plans/LAST-DROP-BYTES.md 7.11), and a door that fenced its caller's N, ISR and block cost 55 bytes of every kern_big'. Only a package that ignores os88spk_init's refusal can pass N=0. Also a correction to the 8088 half: on an IBM ROM the int 0 dummy masks the 8259 (wm.inc:8268-8275), so it does not simply continue there. It is still one of the things gfce-1's panel would name.

findings.title: DESK.DRV's .make divides a package BX fenced only by plausibility
findings.detail: deskmod.inc's .make arm reads [bx+W_FLAGS] and [bx+W_SEG], then does div cl on bx - wm_wins with no range test. The only fence is [bx+W_SEG] == [ld_base] during a load. This is wm-1's shape in a module.
findings.recommendation: Take wm-2's stored W_IDX if it lands; otherwise run wm_isrec's three-instruction bound first.
findings.verify_note: deskmod.inc:236-266: .make tests W_FLAGS, [ld_base] == [bx+W_SEG] and the loading record's I_STATE, then sub ax,wm_wins / div cl with no range test, and indexes wm_owner+si with the unbounded quotient. The fence is plausibility only. Low severity is right: the arm is reachable only from a package's entry proc during a load.

findings.title: SYSTEM.CFG gets a domain column, not per-byte patches
findings.detail: The settings unpack copies every mapped byte raw. Hostility is then each reader's job: the dock clamps, thm_set refuses, and the Date/Time page uses clk_h12 as a count and corrupts .bss (sysmisc-2). The domains are tiny: 0..1 flags, a tier range, bitmasks, and 0..15 colours.
findings.recommendation: Give each CFG_MAP row a MAX byte, and have the unpack read an out-of-domain byte as the default 0 (cmp al,[cs:si-1] / jbe / xor al,al). sysmisc-2's fix becomes one row's MAX, and future count-shaped keys are covered on the day they are added.
findings.bytes_est: ~+22 .ovl and ~+22 CTRL.DRV (15 rows + 7 code on kern_big), 0 resident
findings.verify_note: Confirmed that CFG_BOOT's %1_unpack (driver.inc:4950-4966) copies every mapped byte raw, and that sysmisc-2 (verified) is one consequence. 15 rows on kern_big with DOCK_OPT, 8 otherwise (DRV_CFG_MAPN). Correction to the recommendation: an out-of-domain byte should SKIP the store, so the boot default stands as driver.inc's map header promises ('the default stands'), not store 0 - 0 is not every key's default, and a skip is no larger than a xor. Byte figures are estimates.

findings.title: cmz_jsayx tells a code from a string at 16; fm_errtab has 11 entries
findings.detail: An AX of 11..15 would read the code bytes of osapi_ferr_text as string pointers, which is toast_say's documented failure mode. Only kernel calls feed it today, so the hazard is latent.
findings.recommendation: cmp ax, FM_NERR in place of cmp ax, 16.
findings.verify_note: compress.inc:3416-3420: cmz_jsayx takes AX < 16 as a FERR_* and indexes fm_errtab, which has FM_NERR = 11 entries (files.inc:2401). Both callers (2331, 2680) pass kernel FERR codes today, so it is latent. cmp ax, imm8 encodes the same for 11 and 16: 0 bytes.

findings.title: One error CLASS, not one error NUMBER
findings.recommendation: Now: write the class table into SPEC.md 18.4. Add one SDK preamble sentence: CF=1 is the only universal refusal, and AX=1 means 'not on this kernel'. Flag day: abi-9's AX=1 across families, moving DRV_CALL's xor ax,ax and the bare stc stubs. Do not renumber into one space.
findings.bytes_est: now 0; flag day ~0 to +3 per stub that keeps its own body
findings.listed_as: abi-9, histsys-14; abi-9's flag-day half is not yet an ABI-BREAK-LIST row and should be
findings.verify_note: Every code named in the class mapping exists (DRVE_* in driver.inc, LD_* in loader.inc, FSKE_* in fsck.inc/os88api.inc). abi-9 (verified) confirms the AX=0/AX=1/FERR_PROT/bare-stc refusal shapes. A proposal for SPEC.md 18.4 plus a flag-day item; the observation that abi-9's flag-day half is not an ABI-BREAK-LIST row holds (grep finds no such row).

findings.title: APICHK=1: the checked kernel, concretely
findings.recommendation: Build the knob plus a soak row shaped like smalllaunch: open every package on the system and apps disks under APICHK and fail on any APICHK E9 line. Add an arm to buildmatrix.
findings.prior_art: Windows 3.1 debug KERNEL (RIP), NT checked build
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: the cell macros are at kernel.asm:2425/2442 (OSAPI_SLOT, 8 bytes) and 2495 (OSAPI_RCELL, 6 bytes), so a same-length call/dw substitution is feasible; smalllaunch is at tests/suite.py:12288. A knob proposal; 0 shipped bytes.

findings.title: kern_mega has two fatal panels with two vocabularies
findings.detail: 'STACK OVERFLOW  TASK 04  SP 1A2C  TASKMGR' (sch_dpstr/sch_dphex4) and ' kern_mega FAULT vv err eeee at cccc:iiii sp ssss - reboot ' (mega_fbuf/mega_bhex4). With gfce-1, all three causes can print one line through sch_dpstr: '<WHAT> TASK nn AT cccc:iiii <NAME>' (plus the error code on kern_mega).
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: sch_s_over 'STACK OVERFLOW  TASK ' (sched.inc) and mega_fbuf ' kern_mega FAULT vv err eeee at cccc:iiii sp ssss - reboot ' (mega.inc:14804) are two vocabularies. The -20 .mega estimate is unmeasured.

findings.title: The hung fsx bracket already has an exit: Ctrl-Alt-Del
findings.recommendation: No latch. Correct SPEC.md 53.1's sentence (see mismatches).
findings.verify_note: kbm_isr (mouse.inc:2885-) falls to .chain on every path except kern_mega's stale-byte refusal, and KBM_SCAN only sets kbm_p5 for keypad 5 before falling into .chain, so Del reaches the ROM's int 09h. kern_big's fsx bracket does not touch IVT 09h or IRQ1's mask (fsx.inc's PIC writes are kern_mega's fsx_rdownf). So Ctrl-Alt-Del answers unless the app replaced int 09h or spins at IF = 0. SPEC.md 53.1's sentence is corrected below.

doc_fixes.old_text: `sch_stkdie` is the only `cli`/`hlt` in the kernel, and until §8.8 it printed
doc_fixes.new_text: `sch_stkdie` is the only `cli`/`hlt` in kern_big and kern_small (kern_mega's `mega_fault` is the other, and the `BOOTMARK=1` and `BOOTHALT=` knobs add their own), and until §8.8 it printed
doc_fixes.why: kern_mega's mega_fault does cli and ends in .dead: hlt (kernel/mega.inc, section .mega); BOOTMARK's mark_faulted (kernel.asm:7714-7719) and the BOOTHALT MARK macros (kernel.asm:5294-5298, 5320-5324, 5548-5552) are cli/hlt too. With no knob, kern_big and kern_small have no other cli+hlt stop.

doc_fixes.old_text: FERR_BIG     equ 10              ; larger than the buffer (or than 64KB)
doc_fixes.new_text:
FERR_BIG     equ 10              ; larger than the buffer - or, on a write,
                                 ; than the 32MB a 16-bit sector count can
                                 ; hold (SPEC.md 18.4.1)
doc_fixes.why: Counts are DX:CX and SPEC.md 18.4.1 is 'no 64KB ceiling on either'; the kernel's own twin (kernel/diskw.inc:71-73) says 'larger than the caller's buffer - or, on a write, than the 32MB sector count a 16-bit count can hold'. The line is an equ, not an OSAPI_ %define, so tools/abilock.py strips its comment and the fingerprint does not move.

doc_fixes.new_text:

; 256*WIN_SIZE, taken unsigned, so a BX below the table faults too (its
; clamp bounds the index it returns, so the `wm_owner+si` load is bounded;

doc_fixes.why: wm_ptr2idx (wm.inc ~7260) does sub ax, wm_wins / div cl: the 8-bit quotient overflows at 256*WIN_SIZE, not past 255*WIN_SIZE (offsets 255*WIN_SIZE..256*WIN_SIZE-1 give 255), and a BX below wm_wins wraps high; wm.inc's own clamp comment already says 'only for an offset under 256*WIN_SIZE past wm_wins'. wm_wins is 9FCAh on kern_big and 766Bh on kern_small, so every BX below it does fault. Comment-only.

doc_fixes.old_text:
An app that hangs in the bracket hangs the
  machine — the same truth as any runaway callback, documented rather than
  defended.
doc_fixes.new_text:
An app that hangs in the bracket hangs the
  desktop — the same truth as any runaway callback, documented rather than
  defended. Ctrl-Alt-Del still warm-resets: IRQ1 reaches the ROM's int 09h
  through `kbm_isr`'s chain (§9.6.5), unless the app replaced that vector
  itself or spins with `IF` = 0.
doc_fixes.why: kbm_isr (kernel/mouse.inc:2885-) ends in a far jump to kbm_old9 on every path but kern_mega's stale-byte refusal, and kern_big's bracket leaves IVT 09h and IRQ1's mask alone, so the BIOS warm reset still answers from inside a hung bracket; the scheduler keeps pre-empting, so it is the desktop (the UI task) that hangs, not the machine.
